questions.stem: Events arrive Poisson at rate 2. T = time to the 3rd event. P(T > 1) equals…
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — the 3rd event is still to come after 1 exactly when at most 2 events fell in [0, 1], a Poisson(2) count.
questions.incorrectFeedback: T > 1 means fewer than 3 events by time 1. That count is Poisson(λt) = Poisson(2), so P(T > 1) = P(Poisson(2) ≤ 2).

questions.stem: T has density proportional to t³e^(−2t). What is E[T]?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — shape 4 (t to the power 4 − 1) and rate 2: mean 4/2 = 2.
questions.incorrectFeedback: t³ means shape 4; e^(−2t) means rate 2. Mean = shape/rate = 4/2 = 2.
